title: Sr. Global Alliance Director, OEM, Storage and ISV
description:
As Sr. Global Alliance Director at vCluster Labs , you aren’t just shipping integrations; you are deciding which stack the world’s AI factories get built out of. Every AI factory ships as a stack: servers from an OEM, a validated design, a scheduler, an observability layer, a data platform, a management plane. The tenant isolation layer is the part nobody has solved. Your job is to make sure that layer is already in the OEM’s reference architecture, already in the price book, and already integrated with the ISVs sitting next to us before the customer ever runs a bake-off. Being in the design is worth more than winning the deal, because you win every deal that design produces.
This is a founding, zero-to-one role on a first-year partner program. There is no partner channel to inherit and no team underneath you. You own the number, the agreements behind it, and the product that ships inside someone else’s box.
As Sr. Global Alliance Director your role will include:

• Owning the OEM alliance strategy: You will own the server and systems vendors building validated AI infrastructure designs end to end: strategy, executive alignment, program agreements, and business reviews. You will design and stand up the OEM commercial model (embedded SKUs, unit economics, tiered pricing for bundled and embedded distribution, royalty and per-node constructs, and a standard OEM order template that lets legal review once and the field move fast), then negotiate and close the orders. You will monitor each OEM’s AI factory roadmap to spot the design cycle before it closes, not after.

• Building the ISV portfolio: You will scope, prioritize, and drive integrations with the storage, network, scheduler, observability, security, data, MLOps, and inference vendors whose customers overlap with ours, running it as a portfolio with explicit thresholds, not a queue of requests. You will land vCluster inside ISV and SaaS platforms as the tenant isolation layer, whether the ISV embeds it, resells it, or co-sells it. You will kill integrations that will not produce, and say so early. An ISV embed that does not change the partner’s own roadmap is a logo, not a route.

• Building the sell-with motion: A shipped integration with no joint motion behind it is a cost, not an asset. You will design repeatable co-sell plays on top of every integration that earns one (account mapping, joint solution briefs, field-to-field engagement, deal registration the partner’s sellers actually use), then connect the resulting opportunities to vCluster’s regional sellers, channel partners, and the NVIDIA alliance to close. You take bundles to market through the partner’s own sales motion, not around it.

• Driving technical alignment on both sides: You will represent partner technology requirements inside vCluster Product and Engineering with evidence attached (which accounts, what revenue, what happens if we do nothing), through one front door: licensing, telemetry, air-gapped operation, support boundaries, and lifecycle. You will write the integration specifications and acceptance criteria yourself. Integration work fails on unclear criteria far more often than on technical difficulty, and that clarity is yours to own.

• Building the technology alliance program: You will design and launch the program itself: tiers, technical certification requirements, joint solution briefs, marketplace and private offer paths, and a self-serve path so a small ISV can integrate without you in the loop. The program has to scale past the partners you personally manage.

• Owning the partnership number: You will report partner-influenced pipeline, integration and certification milestones, joint bookings contribution, and field activation to vCluster leadership, with MEDDPICC on every joint opportunity and weekly pipeline inspection. This is a first-year partner program with team MBOs and OKRs; you show up to the weekly inspection with your own numbers, your own forecast, and your own plan to close

title: Forward-Deployed Integrations Engineer
description:
Reports to: Chief Technology Officer
Location: Burlington, VT (hybrid) or remote (no formal travel required)
About OhMD

OhMD is an AI patient communication platform trusted by thousands of healthcare organizations. Our product suite includes two-way patient texting, an AI voice and text assistant that handles inbound patient calls with a human always in the loop, and integrations with the leading ambulatory EHRs, including athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, DrChrono, Elation, and Healthie.
Practices using OhMD reduce inbound call volume by 50% or more, which is the difference between a front desk that is drowning and one that can actually take care of patients.
Why this role exists
Every healthcare organization operates on a unique technology stack.
One EHR exposes a clean FHIR endpoint. Another has a vendor-specific API with its own authentication and rate limits. A third has no supported API at all for the scheduling, patient, or clinical data our product needs. Even practices on the same EHR configure it differently, enforce different security requirements, and run entirely different front-desk workflows.

OhMD still has to work.
Our products need accurate patient context, appointment data, and workflow state to resolve conversations safely. Our AI voice and text assistant cannot book, confirm, or reschedule an appointment it cannot see. Those integrations have to be reliable enough to support real patient interactions, secure enough to handle protected health information, and understandable enough that our customers trust what is happening.
Which brings us to the hard part, and to you.
This role owns the path between a practice's real-world workflow and a working production integration. You'll sit with customers, understand how their systems actually operate, choose the right integration approach, build it, test it, launch it, and stay with it until it works cleanly.
Today that footprint spans more than a dozen EHRs. Our deepest integrations are athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, DrChrono, Elation, and Healthie, and they run across three codebases: a .NET service that handles patient sync and chart write-back, an Elixir platform that handles scheduling and reminders, and a TypeScript and Playwright service for systems that don't offer a usable API. You won't need to be expert in all three on day one, but you will need to be comfortable reading and shipping in each.
Sometimes the right answer will be a vendor REST API or a FHIR application. Sometimes there will be no usable interface at all, and you'll build production-grade browser automation to retrieve the data OhMD needs.
This is not a role where you write a specification and hand it to someone else. You'll be the engineer in the customer conversation and the customer-facing owner in the code.
What your first 90 days look like
Weeks 1-4: Live in the product. Learn how OhMD connects to EHRs today, shadow customer discovery sessions and go-lives, and understand how patient, scheduling, and workflow data move through the platform. Get familiar with our integrations across EHRs.
Weeks 5-8: Own your first integration with support. Scope the customer’s requirements, select the right technical path, build or configure the integration, validate the data, and support the customer through testing. Ship something that runs against a real production workflow.
Weeks 9-12: Lead an integration workstream independently. Own technical discovery, implementation, validation, launch, and early production support. Bring us a point of view on what should become a reusable connector, what belongs in shared infrastructure, and where our current approach will break at scale.
Essential Duties - What You’ll Own
Customer integrations, start to finish
You’ll work directly with healthcare organizations, EHR vendors, internal implementation teams, and engineering partners to understand what a customer needs and how their systems behave.
You’ll translate operational workflows into concrete technical requiremen
